title: Essential Apps for Traveling in Yunnan

basic.summary: A small, practical set of apps for payments, maps, trains, taxis, translation and communication while travelling in Yunnan.

hero.alt: Two hands holding phones displaying the Alipay and WeChat logos

body:
You do not need fifteen new apps for a holiday in Yunnan. You need a small set that can handle payment, directions, transport bookings and communication—and you need to open them before leaving home.

The awkward moment is discovering at Kunming airport that registration needs a text message you cannot receive, or that a train account does not match your passport. Set up the essentials on reliable Wi-Fi and test anything involving payment or identity.

For most independent visitors, six functions are enough. Some can live inside the same app, so the actual number of downloads may be smaller.

<GuideImage src="/images/journeys/攻略/pexels-cottonbro-4543006.jpg" alt="A traveller using a map on a smartphone" />

## Alipay for payment and useful travel services

Alipay is a practical first app. It supports overseas numbers and eligible international cards, subject to identity and bank checks, and also provides access to transport and ride-hailing services.

Complete registration before the trip, then make a small test payment on arrival. The [guide to paying in Yunnan](/travel-guides/how-to-pay-in-yunnan/) covers QR codes, cards and cash.

Do not treat Alipay as a reason to leave your physical card and all cash at the hotel. It is the main tool, not the only backup.

## WeChat for people, with Weixin Pay as a backup

Hotels, guides and drivers often use WeChat for messages, locations and last-minute arrangements. Add important contacts while you still have another way to reach them.

Weixin Pay can be a second payment option, but there is no need to duplicate every service across both apps. WeChat’s main value is connecting you to people.

<GuideImage src="/images/journeys/攻略/9998c76243970e74c6895434ec7393a6.jpeg" alt="Two hands holding phones displaying the Alipay and WeChat logos" />

## Amap for local directions

Amap, also known as Gaode Maps, has useful local place data, road entrances, public transport stops and Chinese addresses. Saved pins make its partly Chinese interface manageable.

Save hotels, stations and the Chinese name of each destination. Check the entrance, not only the pin; old towns and large stations may have widely separated gates.

Keep the hotel’s Chinese address as text and a screenshot for times when the map cannot load.

## China Railway 12306 or Trip.com for trains

China Railway’s 12306 website and app are the official ticket channels. Foreign travellers can verify a passport, buy tickets and manage changes or refunds.

Trip.com is often easier in English and combines trains, flights and accommodation, although third-party conditions and charges may differ. Keep confirmations offline.

Enter passport details exactly and carry the original passport used for booking. A ticket screenshot does not replace it.

<GuideImage src="/images/journeys/攻略/充电宝.png" alt="A traveller charging a phone with a power bank while photographing snow-covered mountains" />

## DiDi or an in-app ride-hailing service

Visitors can use DiDi Greater China or ride services inside Alipay and WeChat. Set up the number and payment method in advance.

Check the pickup point: stations, airports and old-town edges may use designated ride-hailing areas. Match the plate number before getting in.

In smaller towns, a hotel-arranged driver may be simpler than repeatedly moving a pickup pin. Confirm the fare, meeting point and payment method in writing.

## One translation tool that works offline

Choose a translation app with offline language packs, camera translation and saved phrases. Test offline mode before departure.

Save your hotel name, dietary restrictions and any medical note in Chinese. Pleco helps with individual words; camera translation is better for menus and signs.

## Apps you probably do not need

Short-stay visitors rarely need every food-delivery, shopping and review app. Registration time can exceed the convenience they add.

Add a specialist app only when a real need appears. A guesthouse can recommend the correct local service or call a taxi when an app is difficult.

## Set everything up in this order

Several days before departure:

1. Confirm that your phone is unlocked and can receive bank and account messages.
2. Register Alipay and WeChat with the same name shown on your passport where identity is required.
3. Link and test a payment method.
4. Create the train-booking account and complete passport verification.
5. Save hotels, stations and key destinations in your map.
6. Download offline translation data and essential screenshots.
7. Update the apps, then avoid unnecessary account changes immediately before travel.

Also keep a small offline folder containing passport copies, insurance details, hotel addresses, transport confirmations and emergency contacts. The phone should make the journey easier, but the whole journey should not disappear when the signal does.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a Chinese mobile number for these apps?

Many core services now accept an overseas number, including major payment and travel apps. Some local mini programs and Wi-Fi portals may still work better with a Chinese number. Check the current registration screen for your account rather than assuming every feature is available.

### Is 12306 better than Trip.com?

12306 is the official railway channel and gives direct control over the booking. Trip.com may be easier in English and useful for a mixed flight-and-train trip. Either can work; accurate passport information matters more than the logo on the app.

### Should I install every app before arriving?

Install and register the essential ones. Leave optional local services until you know you need them. Fewer working accounts are better than a crowded phone full of apps that were never tested.

## Official references

* [China Government: Guide to Working and Living in China](https://english.www.gov.cn/2025special/bizexpatsinchina2025)
* [China Railway 12306: English website FAQ](https://www.12306.cn/en/faq.html)
* [China Government: Digital services for overseas visitors](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202602/05/content_WS69849d8ac6d00ca5f9a08eff.html)

App availability, language support and registration rules change. Recheck each service before publication and future updates.
